title: Quesadillas
equipment: Rimmed sheet pan (to keep them warm)

items: 1½ cups shredded cooked chicken, or 1 can (16 oz) refried beans

steps: Heat the oven to 200°F and put a rimmed sheet pan inside. It keeps finished quesadillas warm while you cook the rest.
Warm the chicken or beans in the microwave 1 min, so the middle heats through in the pan.
Lay the tortillas flat. Spread or scatter a quarter of the chicken or beans over one half of each tortilla. Top with ½ cup cheese and fold the bare half over.
Melt about 1½ tsp butter in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 or 2 quesadillas.

Cook 2–3 min, until the bottom is golden brown. Flip with a wide spatula and cook 2–3 min more, until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted. If the outside browns before the cheese melts, lower the heat a little.
Move to the sheet pan in the oven. Repeat with the rest, adding butter for each one.
Rest 1 min, then cut each into 3 wedges. Serve with sour cream and salsa on the side.
tips: Leftover taco meat, black beans or sautéed peppers and onions all work as fillings.
For a crowd, bake them. Brush the outsides with melted butter and bake on a sheet pan at 425°F for 10–12 min, flipping once.
storage: Best fresh. Leftovers keep in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a dry skillet over medium-low heat 3–4 min per side, or in an air fryer at 350°F for 4–5 min, until hot and crisp.
